Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Aule Studenti <gu...@uni-bocconi.it> writes:
>Hi to every one,
>cause I'm a novice of this game,I would know how i can control a
>vampire, because in the rules book say that there is a number in the
>right-upper corner, but there is nothing so I have thought that is the
>number in the red circle in the right-lower corner...

Correct.

>Another question..
>When I use some blood counters to control (using a verb of Magic: "Cast
>a vampire") a vampire, that blood point return to me or they are lost
>for ever...

The blood pool spent on (transferred to) a vampire is kept by the
vampire when it becomes controlled (is "cast"). The counters
then represent that vampire's blood - which he can spend (burn)
to play certain cards, to heal damage, etc.

Messages.Author: Pheersum
Messages.Body:
During the influence phase of your turn you may spend your four
transfers to move blood from your pool onto an uncontrolled vampire in
your inactive region (one blood per transfer), move blood from
uncontrolled vampire to pool (one blood uses two transfers up), or spend
one blood & all four transfers to bring a vampire from the crypt
(vampire card draw pile) into the inactive region.
At the end of this phase any vampires with blood counters equal to its
capacity (the number in the red circle in the lower-right of a vampire
card) is brought out face up into the controlled region with the blood
on it.
The blood is then used to pay for effects of certain minion cards. If a
minion card or combat card has a white filled blood drop on the left
border that blood is payed by the vampire, and the vampire can later
hunt as an action to regain blood to pay for more effects. But I
digress...
I hope this is useful, and I hope you find this newsgroup of help, and
enjoy the game.
-eric
